17; History
18;
19; Version 01
20; 05/24/07 - Appears to compile corerctly !
21;
22; Version 02
23; 05/24/07 - Change calibration data to match my cal (2.5 T1 ver6)
24; For reference, my car runs a stock (blueprinted) 2.5 T1, with
25; mitsu turbo 16psi boost, +20 injectors and a 3-bar MAP. This
26; should be a good base cal for just about any 2.5 T1 cars.
27;
28; Version 03
29; 05/25/07 - Changed Baud Rate references to 3 constants; added option to
30; enable/disable serial interrupt routine (hi-speed logger); changed
31; the MAP transfer function values to a constant rather than hard-
32; coded.
33;
34; Version 04
35; 06/29/07 - Fixed the staging mod switch reference.
36;
37; Version 05
38; 06/29/07 - Modified the PumpEff calculation code to re-scale the table to
39; 50-150%.
40;
41; Version 06
42; 08/01/07 - Cleaned up stuff; added injector scaling info to table defs.
43;
44; Version 07
45; 08/09/07 - Added anti-lag code.
46;
47; Version 08
48; 08/13/07 - More cleanup; added ChEM2 calx definitions; changed fan control
49; speeds to be tuneable via constants rather than hard-coded.
50; Version 09
51; 09/12/07 - Added routine for 2-stage shift light control. Added constants
52; and variables for shift light control.
53;
54; Version 10
55; 10/16/07 - Fixed the brclr/brset instructions that referenced the config
56; constant.
57; * Starts and runs the car, finally. But, ASD will not turn off
58; after key-on. Will not flash codes. CEL is always on also.
59; * Staging Limiter tested - OK
60; * Hi-Speed logger tested - OK
61;
62; Version 11 --- First Public Release ---
63; 03/12/08 - Added assembler switches for ATX/MTX to simplify setup.
64; Added 2/3-Bar switches to assy source.
65; Source cal changed to MP 353 (for ATX) and 131 (for MTX).
66; Fixed Anti-Lag code (bad conditional branch instruction).
67; Fixed ldx (0x000e <-- 0x000d) in the 'zeroram from 3 to ff' routine.
68; Found and fixed an error in the Cruise Control Routine.
69; Found and fixed an assembler directive error in the switchable boost
70; polarity check code.
71; Fixed a code error (related to my original cal) in the Cruise routine
72; Fixed a couple of hard-coded MAP references to be configurable with
73; MAP changes.
74; Added charge temp sensor enable to config flags
75; * ASD cycle is working correctly now
76; * CE light displays codes correctly
77;
78; Version 12
79; 04/21/08 - Removed the Baro add in the Anti-Lag retard routine. BoostTarget is
80; actually a MAP target (baro is already added in) so, adding in Baro
81; was causing an overlow and incorreclty calculating the Anti-Lag.
82; - Fixed some .tbl file definitions that caused crashing problems with
83; D-Cal.
84; - Added in calibration values for 2.2l enigne (copied from T2 where
85; applicable), and added in assembler switch to build 2.2 version.
86;
87; Version 13
88; 06/04/08 - There were a couple of constants from the MP MTX cal that caused
89; the spark scatter to be inhibited in the MTX build. So, I changed
90; these back to stock (same value as the ATX). It caused the idle to
91; remain high during gear shifts. Probably added by Mopar to the MTX
92; cal for road racing.
93; - Returned the 2.2l cal O2 ramps and adaptive cells back to stock
94; from the MP T2 (which tends to run rich due to the ramp
95; calibration).
96; - Added polarity switch for Staging Limiter.
97; - Added assembler option for WG control and a NEW T2-style WG control
98; routine. This routine is functioanlly similar to the T2 WG routine.
99; But, it's actually a modification of the T1 routine to invert the
100; duty cycle so that the T2 style WG plumbing can be used. The T1 WG
101; routine is tied into the knock retard system, so it would be
102; impossible to simply paste the T2 WG control into Turbonator. The
103; T2 WG duty cycle tables are copied over from the T2 cal to be used
104; as a baseline.
105; - Created a 3rd option for WG control. A custom routine based on the
106; T1 code but with some modifications so that it can be used with a
107; T2 style WG system (source control), but with a failsafe mode.
108; Similar to the T3 WG control in that regard. Also added an
109; additional lookup for this routine that increases the WG DC based
110; on the delta to boost goal. This should help spoolup by maximizing
111; the DC during transient conditions.
112; - Changed the switchable boost implementation to a constant for lo-
113; boost instead of a table.
114; - Separated the Boost and WG Duty Cycle lookups to make it easier to
115; implement the T2 and Turbonator Custom WG control routines.
116; - Fixed a flag reference error in the speed calculation that caused
117; the speed to not update properly past 24mph.
118;
119; Version 14
120; 08/07/08 - Found and fixed 2 fan control jumps.
121; - Found and fixed and error in the DRB memory location table.
122; - Found and fixed a DRB memroy table reference error.
123; - Found and fixed a DRB Switch test table reference error.
124; - Found and fixed a dis-assy error in the Spark Scatter Idle routine.
125; This was probably the cause of the rough/rich idle.
126;
127; Version 14.5
128; 10/02/08 - Moved the flag location for the Turbonator Staging limiter due to
129; a previously undetected overlap with the cruise control routine.
130; This hopefully fixes the mystery mis-fire.
131; - Fixed the constant definition for the PIA output masks. This
132; constant can be used to mask fault codes associated with the
133; various PIA output bits.
134; - Deleted all of the boost control routines except the 'Turbonator'
135; boost control (modified, anti-lag version of the T1).
136;
137; Version 14.6
138; 10/31/08 - Fixed a typo for the Staging Limiter/Misfire fix above.
139;
140; Version 14.7
141; 11/13/08 - Fixed calibration values for P/T enrichment and spark scatter fuel.
142; - Added proper 2.2 calibration values for the same.
143;
144; Version 14.8
145; 12/01/08 - Fixed calibration value for THRMAX for ATX (0x23 <-- 0x75).
146; - Made the anti-lag inclusion more robust. There was a possibility
147; it would be ignored.
148;
149; Version 14.9
150; 01/06/09 - Fixed an arror in the AmbientTempSensor Fault detection routine that
151; probably caused a battery charging error I've had (but noone else
152; reported).
153; - Fixed a MAP scaling error with the RPMMAP table. This is not
154; actually a MAP-based table and should not have been scaled.
155;
156; Version 15
157; 02/18/09 - Moved the calibration data to a template file for simplicity. All
158; calibration options will now be handled by changing the tempalte
159; file instead of assembler options (.if statements). Though, MAP
160; changes will still be handled by .if statements.
161; - Adated PTU Control routine from TBI/V6 SMEC using data tables from
162; '90/91 SBEC T1 cars (same as 'leftover' data in the '89 T1 code.
163; There is an overlap with the EMR control that must be disabled by
164; flags.
165; - Removed the T1 and T2 boost control option (T2 never really worked
166; right). The only option now is Turbonator. You can get to the
167; 'stock' T1 boost control by setting the table
168; 'DCWBST_FullThrottleWastegateDutyCycleAdjustment_FromBoostTarget'
169; to return zero for all inputs.
170; - Added a 2nd option flags so that I can add a spark-based rev
171; limiter. It's not working yet, but at least the code is
172; structured for it.
173;
174; Version 15.1
175; 02/27/09 - Fixed the Spark-based rev limiter code. Waiting to test.
176;
177; Version 15.2
178; 03/30/09 - Corrected the jump for the staging limiter (to check for the
179; option, was bypassed previously - I forgot to change it...)
180;
181; Version 15.3
182; 09/02/09 - Corrected the template files for the aftermarket scantool codes.
183; These were previously unknown codes (to me) and were commented out
184; of the assembly. I added them back in and included a de-coder.
185; However, since this codebase is based on the '89 T1 (and the
186; memory loations and DRB routines are as such), the codes need to
187; stay unchanged.
188;
189; Version 16.0
190; 09/22/09 - Removed all .if switches and added/corrected table definitions for
191; compatibility with MP Tune. The .if switches have been simply
192; commented out. So, if you prefer to use CHeMAsm instead of
193; MP Tuner, you will need to remove the comments.
194; - Added template definitions for S60, and Masi 8V ATX.
195; - Fixed several constant definitions, table definitions, and some
196; cal data. Too numerous to detail each change...
197;
198; Version 16.1
199; 01/27/10 - Removed the 150% PumpEff Rescale code and reverted it back to
200; stock. This was apparently had a math error that caused an
201; overflow that in turn caused the misfire problem.
202;
203; Version 16.2
204; 02/01/10 - Fixed an error in the WG Control routine that was causing the
205; wrong WGDC to be calculated. This was caused when I separated the
206; boost lookup from the WGDC calculation.
207;
208; Version 16.3
209; 02/16/10 - Updated all of the templates to improve the grouping and to take
210; advantage of the new ramp editor in MP Tuner (table type 11).
211;
212; Version 16.4
213; 06/02/10 - Updated the Anti-Lag code to keep it from activating when in
214; vacuum.
215; - Updated the Charge Temp Sens Enable code to force a zero return
216; for the fuel table.
217; - Updated the shift light code to be more simple, single setpoint
218; style. Same code as T-LM.
219;
220; Version 16.5
221; 07/28/10 - Fixed the PWADD table for the 2.2 templates.
222; Added the dwell time from battery volts lookup from the Mexican
223; SBEC cals. Should make for more consistent spark.
224;
225; Version 16.6
226; 08/17/10 - Changed the Dwell calculation to be more like stock. The Mexican
227; lookup did not work correctly in this code. Added a constant for
228; minimum anti-dwell period (MINADW) to allow fine tuning.
229;
230; Version 16.7
231; 08/24/10 - Added WOT battery volts target. Allows you to either dis-able (by
232; setting the targetlow) or step-up (by setting higher) the
233; alternator output when at WOT.
234; - Added MAPFLR to MAP scaling list. This may be a contributor to
235; engine stall when the CTS is unplugged.
236; - Reconfigured how the charge temp sesnor is enabled/disabled. This
237; likely is the cause of the engine stall when the CTS is unplugged.
238;
239; Version 16.8
240; 10/17/10 - Fixed the bypass code for thecharge temp sensor (again). The way
241; I did it in 16.7 obviously wasn't right as it did not work
242; correctly.
243; - Removed the WOTBAT target since it seems to be causing a no-start
244; condition.
245;
246; Version 16.9
247; 10/26/10 - Added PTU Routine to the main program loop so that it can run.
248; - Changed (again) the charge temp code to fix the stalling issue.
249;
250; Version 17.0
251; 05/17/11 - Changed template format for MPT2.
252; - Removed the EMR Routine for space/execution time.
253; - Removed the CCD bus routine for space/execution time.
254;
255; Version 17.1
256; 08/11/11 - Updated staging limiter to work when no switch is selected.
257; - Updated scaling for AESLOP (transient fuel).
258;
259; Version 17.2
260; 12/17/11 - Testing spark cut rev limiter again...

263; 04/30/12 - Completely re-written anti-lag and staging limiter.
264; - Anti-lag now goes to a single pre-set value rather than a
265; retard value.
266; - Anti-lag comes on at user-set RPM level.
267; - Staging limiter now has spark cut option. Spark cut is
268; rotating and has a selectable fraction.
269;

271; 06/05/12 - Added T2-type boost control.
272; 06/26/12 - Fixed an error in the calling routine for the T2 Boost Control.
273; - Fixed the MAP scaling for the T2 boost-control tables
274; - Updated the T2 WGDC to match the T2 (or base cal) where appropriate.
275;

277; 01/01/13 - Fixed a table reference in the PTU code.
278; - Changed the PTU table naming to more accurately reflect the useage.
279; - Fixed a calculation in the Anit-lag code for negative values.
280;

282; 01/04/13 - Complete re-write of the launch control. Launch control is now a
283; separate routine.
284; - Added Decel Fuel Cut code to completely turn off the injectors on
285; decel.
286; - Updated the spark-cut rev limiter code to work better.
287; - Re-adopted 150% PEFTBL Scale. Working now.
288;
289; Verison 19.1
290; 01/06/13 - Fixed code for the rotating spark cut counter.
291;
292; Version 19.2
293; 01/07/13 - Fixed code for the decel fuel cut that prevented it from running.

296; - Added TPS Threshold for staging to prevent WOT fuelling at idle

299; 09/11/13 - Fixed boost control type switch (T1/T2). The error caused the

331; *****************************************************************************
332; Calibration Template definition
333; *****************************************************************************
334;
335; This template format will be used from T-SMEC v15 and later.
336;
337; I decided to switch to this format because it was getting clumsy
338; trying to define the switches for all of the build options (MTX/ATX,
339; 2.2/2.5, boost control, etc.). This way, all the calibration data can be
340; kept together in 1 place.
341;
342; T-SBEC will have it's own template format and the 2 CAN NOT be
343; interchanged. This is due to the different code structures between the
344; SMEC and SBEC.
345;
346;
347; Filename format:
348;
349; T-SMEC_[displ]_[trans]_[ID]_[version].asm
350;
351; For example, the 1st tempalte file I made was from the 89 T1 Auto:
352;
353; T-SMEC_25_ATX_a139_stock.asm
354;
355; This way you can start your T-SMEC build with any calibration.
356;
357; !!! This line is now written by MP Tuner when you specify the template to build with. !!!
358

361; ***********************************************************************
362;
363; Bit functions:
364; Many bytes in the RAM contain status bits. For each of these the address value
365; was separated into bit numbers, for example Flags_50 has b50_bit7 through b50_bit0.
366; As the function of the bits was decoded, a global replace was performed to replace
367; the bit name with a meaningful name, like:
368;
369; b50_SparkEngineNotRunning = $%10000000 ; -10000000-
370;
371; When working with bits, you can add several together using the "or" operator | like this:
372;
373; b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized ; -10100000-
374;
375; The inverse function ~ sets all bits except the ones specified, so:
376;
377; ~b50_SparkEngineNotRunning ; -01111111-
378;
379; You can combine the inverse ~ with the or | like this:
380;
381; ~(b50_SparkEngineNotRunning | b50_BaroSolEnergized) ; -01011111-
382;
383; The intent here was to make the logical functionality of the code easier to follow.
384;
385; ***********************************************************************
386;

388; 1989 Turbo I
389;

1239; The OC1 timer is setup in 2's complement form so that it could run faster, but that the minimum is 32289us or 32.3ms
1240 
1241Interrupt_TimerOutputCapture1:
1242 ldaa #CPU_TIFlag1_OutputCompare1 ; load a with value -10000000-
1243 staa CPU_TimerInterruptFlag1
1244 ldaa #0x10 ; load a with value -00010000-
1245 staa CPU_A2DControlReg
1246 ldd CPU_Timer_OC1
1247 addd #0x01df ; 479us
1248 cmpD CPU_TimerCounterRegHigh ; compare D
1249 bpl L1000 ; branch if plus (hi bit 0)
1250 ldd CPU_TimerCounterRegHigh
1251 addd #0x01df ; 479 microseconds...
1252L1000: addd #0x0002 ; 481 microseconds...
1253 std CPU_Timer_OC1
1254 ldaa CPU_TimerInterruptMask1 ; load a with memory contents
1255 anda #0x7f ; AND a with value -01111111-
1256 staa CPU_TimerInterruptMask1
1257 ldaa Timer_AlternatorDutyCycle ; load a with memory contents
1258 inca ; increment a
1259 staa Timer_AlternatorDutyCycle ; store a into memory

1261; How the Fuel Monitor works:
1262; (Geoff Allan)
1263; The "Navigator" module in the dash receives a signal for every engine rotation. The
1264; length of time of this signal is dependent on the injector open duration. This gives
1265; the Navigator the ability to precisely calculate how much fuel is being used for a
1266; given time or distance, since it now has RPM and injector duty cycle in addition to
1267; being tapped into the speed/distance sensor. In order to
1268; accomodate differing injector sizes, the Conversion factor can be changed. Stock T1
1269; conversion factor is $03a8, if you scale the injectors you need to scale this value
1270; by the same amount so the Navigator retains its accuracy.
1271 
1272 ldd Timer_FuelMonitorOutputTimer_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
1273 subd FUELTR_FuelMonitorConversionFactor ; (data is 03a8) = 0.936ms
1274 bcs L1001 ; branch if lower
1275 stD *Timer_FuelMonitorOutputTimer_HB ; store D to RAM
1276 ldaa PIA2_PortA_DataDirection ; load a with memory contents
1277 eora #0x08 ; XOR a with value -00001000-
1278 staa PIA2_PortA_DataDirection
1279L1001: cli ; enable interrupts
1280 ldaa Timer_AlternatorDutyCycle ; load a with memory contents
1281 lsra
1282 bcc ControlAlternator ; branch if greater or equal
1283 jmp L1013
1284 
1285ControlAlternator:
1286 ldaa ATMOffset ; load a with memory contents
1287 cmpa #0x0d ; compare a with value -00001101-
1288 beq L1010 ; branch if equal (zero)
1289 cmpa #0x14 ; compare a with value -00010100-
1290 beq L1010 ; branch if equal (zero)
1291 ldx #PIA2_PortB_DataDirection ; load index with value
1292 brset *BitFlags_54, #b54_FuelEngineNotRunning, TurnAlternatorOff ; branch if bit(s) set
1293 ldab #0x11 ; load b with value -00010001- (546 rpm) min alternator rpm?
1294 brset *BitFlags_56, #b56_BadASD, L1002 ; branch if bit(s) set
1295 ldab #0x15 ; load b with value -00010101- (674 rpm)
1296L1002: bclr *BitFlags_56, #b56_BadASD ; clear bits
1297 cmpb EngineRpm_HB
1298 bhi TurnAlternatorOff ; branch if higher
1299 bset *BitFlags_56, #b56_BadASD ; set bits
1300 ldaa CPU_A2DResults2 ; load a with memory contents
1301 cmpa BatteryVolts ; compare a with memory contents
1302 bcc L1003 ; branch if greater or equal
1303 staa BatteryVolts ; store a into memory
1304L1003: cmpa #0x41 ; compare a with value -01000001-
1305 bcc L1004 ; branch if greater or equal
1306 ldab Counter_MainLoop ; load b with memory contents
1307 bitb #0x06 ; -00000110-
1308 bne TurnAlternatorOff ; branch if not equal (not zero)
1309L1004: brclr 0, X, #pia2b_AlternatorField, L1005 ; branch if bit(s) clear
1310 brclr 0, X, #pia2b_bit2, L1011 ; branch if bit(s) clear
1311 bclr *BitFlags_56, #b56_AlternatorBits ; clear bits
1312L1005: suba TargetBatteryVolts
1313 bne L1006 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
1314 brclr 0, X, #pia2b_AlternatorField, TurnAlternatorOn ; branch if bit(s) clear
1315 bra TurnAlternatorOff ; branch
1316 
1317L1006: ldab #0x0e ; load b with value -00001110-
1318 bcc L1008 ; branch if greater or equal
1319 nega ; negate a (set high bit)
1320 cmpa #0x02 ; compare a with value -00000010-
1321 beq L1007 ; branch if equal (zero)
1322 bcc TurnAlternatorOn ; branch if greater or equal
1323 ldab #0x06 ; load b with value -00000110-
1324L1007: andb Timer_AlternatorDutyCycle
1325 beq TurnAlternatorOff ; branch if equal (zero)
1326 bra TurnAlternatorOn ; branch
1327 
1328L1008: cmpa #0x02 ; compare a with value -00000010-
1329 beq L1009 ; branch if equal (zero)
1330 bcc TurnAlternatorOff ; branch if greater or equal
1331 ldab #0x06 ; load b with value -00000110-
1332L1009: andb Timer_AlternatorDutyCycle

1341 bcs L1012 ; branch if lower

1343 bset *BitFlags_47, #b47_Alternator ; set bits
1344 bra TurnAlternatorOff ; branch

1359; How the AIS drive works:
1360; (Geoff Allan)
1361; A stepper motor has a combination of electromagnetic fields that cause it to only
1362; rotate a tiny amount at a time. There are 4 wires going to the AIS stepper. In order
1363; to complete a step, there must be two distinct patterns of bits sent to these 4 wires
1364; after a short delay to account for the mechanical movement involved. It is possible
1365; that the computer has requested a new AIS position that is several steps away from the
1366; current position. This routine continues sending the patterns required to move the
1367; AIS motor to the desired new position.

2539; CCD Bus operation description - The bus sends 2 bytes at a time down the SPI. The first byte
2540; is the ID code of the data being sent, the 2nd byte is the actual data.
2541;
2542; How to add data to bus? Maybe read the later models bus protocol...
2543;
2544; HandleCCDBusComs:
2545; sei ; disable interrupts
2546; ldaa PIA2_PortA_DataDirection ; load a with memory contents
2547; bita #pia2a_CCDBus ; enable the CCD Bus chip
2548; bne R1166 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
2549; brset *CCDVar0, #ccd_Bit7, CCD_Error ; branch if bit(s) set
2550; ldd CCDTemp_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
2551; bsr CCD_XmitCode ; call subroutine
2552; cmpD CCDTemp_HB ; compare D
2553; beq L1167 ; branch if equal (zero)
2554; ldx #PIA2_PortA_DataDirection ; load index with value
2555; brset 0, X, #pia2a_CCDBus, R1166 ; branch if bit(s) set
2556; ldab 0x01,x ; load b with memory at index + value
2557; bset 1, X, #$%00000100 ; bit set
2558; bclr 0, X, #$%00000001 ; bit clear
2559; bclr 1, X, #$%00000100 ; bit clear
2560; bset 0, X, #$%00000001 ; bit set
2561; bclr 0, X, #$%00000001 ; bit clear
2562; stab 0x01,x
2563; bra L1165 ; branch
2564;
2565; CCD_Error:
2566; ldd #0xffff ; load d (a&b) with value -11111111 11111111-
2567; bsr CCD_XmitCode ; call subroutine
2568; L1165: cmpa #0xaa ; check the response
2569; bne R1166 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
2570; bset *CCDFlags2, #$%00100000 ; set error flag?
2571; R1166: rts ; return from subroutine
2572;
2573; L1167: cmpa #0x84 ; compare CCDTemp_HB to 0x84
2574; bne L1168 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
2575; ldab CCDFlags3 ; load b with memory contents
2576; bpl L1168 ; branch if plus (hi bit 0)
2577; andb #0x7f ; -01111111- was set, so now clear bit 7, in B
2578; clr CCDFlags3 ; zero byte at memory location ; clear all flags
2579; ldaa #0xc4 ; load a with value -11000100-
2580; stD *CCDTemp_HB ; store D to RAM
2581; bra R1169 ; branch
2582;
2583; L1168: bset *CCDVar0, #ccd_Bit7 ; set error bit
2584; R1169: rts ; return from subroutine
2585;
2586; CCD_XmitCode:
2587; cmpb CPU_SerialPeripheralStatus ; status must be checked before data is read, this command only readies the data to be read, I think
2588; staa CPU_SerialPeripheralDataIO
2589; ldx #CPU_SerialPeripheralStatus ; load index with value
2590; ldY #0x0005 ; load Y index -00000000 00000101-
2591; L1170: brset 0, X, #bit_bit7, CCD_XmitData ; branch if SPIF (xfer complete) flag is set
2592; deY ; decrement Y
2593; bne L1170 ; loop until transfer is complete or times out
2594; rts ; return from subroutine
2595;
2596; CCD_XmitData:
2597; ldaa CPU_SerialPeripheralDataIO ; load a with memory contents
2598; stab CPU_SerialPeripheralDataIO ; store b into memory
2599; ldY #0x0005 ; load Y index -00000000 00000101-
2600; L1172: brset 0, X, #bit_bit7, CCD_ReadResult ; branch if SPIF (xfer complete) flag is set
2601; deY ; decrement Y
2602; bne L1172 ; loop until transfer is complete or times out
2603; rts ; return from subroutine
2604;
2605; CCD_ReadResult:
2606; ldab CPU_SerialPeripheralDataIO ; just to clear the buffer, this value is never used or stored
2607; rts ; return from subroutine
2608

3240 brset *BitFlags_4f, #b4f_OffIdle, FindCruiseCell ; branch if bit(s) set
3241 ldab #0x16 ; Point to the idle cell...
3242 bra DecideRichOrLeanValue ; branch
3243 
3244FindCruiseCell:
3245 clrb ; b = 0
3246 ldaa EngineRpm_HB ; load a with memory contents
3247FindRPMCell:
3248 cmpa 0x00,x ; compare a with memory at index + value
3249 bcs CheckRPMCell ; branch if RPM cell boundary is greater than actual RPM
3250 incb ; b=b+1
3251 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
3252 cmpb #0x02 ; 3 looops only
3253 bcs FindRPMCell ; branch if lower
3254 bra L1234 ; branch if end of RPM range
3255 
3256CheckRPMCell:
3257 tstb
3258 bne L1233 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
3259 inx ;
3260L1233: inx ; point to the MAP cells
3261L1234: ldaa MapValue ; load a with memory contents
3262FindMAPCell:
3263 cmpa 0x00,x ; compare a with memory at index + value
3264 bcs L1236 ; branch if MAP cell boundary is lower than actual MAP
3265 addb #0x03 ; -00000011-
3266 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
3267 cmpb #0x06 ; -00000110-
3268 bcs FindMAPCell ; branch if lower
3269 bra L1238 ; branch if end of MAP range
3270 
3271L1236: cmpb #0x03 ; -00000011-
3272 bcc L1237 ; branch if greater or equal
3273 inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
3274L1237: inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
3275L1238: lslb
3276DecideRichOrLeanValue:
3277 brclr *BitFlags_4f, #b4f_O2Rich, LoadCellValue ; branch if bit(s) clear
3278 incb
3279LoadCellValue:
3280 abx ; add b to index
3281 ldaa 0x14,x ; load a with memory at index + value
3282 tab ; b = a
3283 rts ; return from subroutine
3284 
3285;
3286; Return values:
3287; - A and B contain the limit value for the selected cell, rich/lean
3288; - X contains the address to the kick value for the selected cell, rich/lean

3291AdaptiveMemory_UpdateCellIfRequired_MM:
3292; Long Term Fuel Trim (LTFT) Update logic. Periodically applies the Short Term Fuel Trim
3293; (Counter_PrimaryAndSecondaryRamp) to the active AutoCalCell (Adaptive Memory).
3294 ldx #AutoCalCell0 ; load index with value
3295 ldab PointerIntoAdaptiveMemory ; load b with memory contents (Get active cell index 0-12)
3296 abx ; add b to index (X now points directly to the active AutoCalCell in memory)
3297 ldab AMUPDT_EPPsBetweenCalChangeUpdateOpenThrottle ; load b with memory contents (data is 1a)
3298 brset *BitFlags_4f, #b4f_OffIdle, UpdateAdaptive_OffIdle ; branch if bit(s) set
3299 ldab AMUPDI_EPPsBetweenCalChangeUpdateClosedThrottle ; load b with memory contents (data is 1a) (Use idle timer threshold if idle)
3300UpdateAdaptive_OffIdle:
3301 brset *BitFlags_50, #b50_OpenLoop, DontUpdateCell_MaybeUpdateTimer ; branch if bit(s) set (Don't adapt in Open Loop)
3302 stab Temp0 ; store b into memory (Threshold timer limit)
3303 ldd InjectorPulsewidth_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
3304 addd Pulsewidth_PartThrottleEnrichment_HB ; d = d + memory contents
3305 subd PWMIN_NoCellUpdateBelow_PWMIN_Pulsewidth ; (data is 0113) (Make sure pulse width is above minimum threshold to allow update)
3306 ldab Temp0 ; load b with memory contents
3307 bcs DontUpdateCell_MaybeUpdateTimer ; branch if lower
3308 sei ; disable interrupts
3309 ldaa AdaptiveCellUpdateTimer_IncrementedEveryDistRisingEdge ; load a with memory contents
3310 sba ; subtract (a=a-b) (Has timer exceeded the threshold?)
3311 bcs DontUpdateCellOrTimer ; branch if lower (Timer not reached yet)
3312 staa AdaptiveCellUpdateTimer_IncrementedEveryDistRisingEdge ; store a into memory (Reset/Decrement timer)
3313 cli ; enable interrupts
3314 ldaa CELCHG_BitsChangePerUpdateWithinACell ; load a with memory contents (data is 01) (How much to shift LTFT per update)
3315 ldab Counter_PrimaryAndSecondaryRamp ; load b with memory contents (Read the Short Term Fuel Trim value)
3316 bpl L1241 ; branch if plus (hi bit 0) (If STFT is positive, meaning engine is running lean, need to increase LTFT)
3317 nega ; negate a (set high bit) (If STFT is negative, meaning engine is running rich, negate step to decrease LTFT)
3318L1241: ldab AMLIMH_MaxMultiplierCannotBeAbove7F ; load b with memory contents (data is 7f)
3319 adda 0x00,x ; Add step to current AutoCalCell value
3320 bvc Adaptive_Overflowed ; branch if overflow
3321 ldaa 0x00,x ; load a with memory at index + value (Restore if overflow)
3322 bpl Adaptive_SetCellToMaxOrMinValue ; branch if plus (hi bit 0)
3323 ldab AMLIML_MinMultiplierCannotBeBelow80 ; load b with memory contents (data is b3)
3324 bra Adaptive_SetCellToMaxOrMinValue ; branch
3325 
3326Adaptive_Overflowed:
3327 cba ; Compare updated cell to upper limit
3328 bge Adaptive_SetCellToMaxOrMinValue ; branch if greater or equal (If too high, cap it)
3329 ldab AMLIML_MinMultiplierCannotBeBelow80 ; load b with memory contents (data is b3)
3330 cba ; Compare updated cell to lower limit
3331 bge L1242 ; branch if greater or equal
3332Adaptive_SetCellToMaxOrMinValue:
3333 tba ; a = b (Apply cap)
3334L1242: staa 0x00,x ; Save updated value back into AutoCalCell
3335DontUpdateCellOrTimer:
3336 cli ; enable interrupts
3337 ldaa 0x00,x ; load a with memory at index + value
3338 staa ValueFromAdaptiveMemory ; store a into memory
3339 rts ; return from subroutine
3340 
3341DontUpdateCell_MaybeUpdateTimer:
3342 ldaa 0x00,x ; load a with memory at index + value
3343 staa ValueFromAdaptiveMemory ; store a into memory
3344 ldaa AdaptiveCellUpdateTimer_IncrementedEveryDistRisingEdge ; load a with memory contents
3345 cba
3346 bcs R1243 ; branch if lower
3347 stab AdaptiveCellUpdateTimer_IncrementedEveryDistRisingEdge ; store b into memory
3348R1243: rts ; return from subroutine
3349 
3350AdaptiveMemory_DetermineWhichCellApplies_MM:
3351; Determines which of the 13 AutoCalCells (0-11 for run, 12 for idle) is currently active based on RPM and MAP.
3352 clra ; a = 0
3353 staa Temp0 ; store a into memory
3354 ldx #MP1_AutoCalMapCellBoundary1 ; load index with value (Base of MAP boundaries)
3355 ldaa BitFlags_4f ; load a with memory contents
3356 bmi ONTHROTTLE_OR_RPMTOOHIGHFORIDLE ; branch if minus(hi bit 1) (If OffIdle is set, skip idle check)
3357 ldab #0x0c ; load b with value -00001100- (Cell 12 is the Idle Cell)
3358 ldaa TargetIdleSpeed_HB ; load a with memory contents
3359 adda IDLOFS_DeltaForIdleRPMForClosedThrottleCell ; (data is 04)
3360 cmpb PointerIntoAdaptiveMemory
3361 bne L1244 ; branch if not equal (not zero) (If already in Cell 12, add hysteresis)
3362 adda HYTRPM_HysteresisFor_IDLOFS ; (data is 02)
3363L1244: cmpa EngineRpm_HB ; compare a with memory contents (Check if RPM is below threshold for idle cell)
3364 bcs ONTHROTTLE_OR_RPMTOOHIGHFORIDLE ; branch if lower (If RPM is too high, it's not idle, use run cells)
3365 bra L1250 ; branch (RPM is low enough, set cell to 12)
3366 
3367L1245: ldaa 0x00,x ; load a with memory at index + value (Load MAP boundary)
3368 cmpb Temp0
3369 bcc L1246 ; branch if greater or equal
3370 adda DLTMAP_MapHysteresisAtMapCellBoundaries ; (data is 01) (Add hysteresis if jumping cells)
3371L1246: cmpa MapValue ; compare a with memory contents
3372 bcc L1247 ; branch if greater or equal (Found our MAP band)
3373 inx ; increment index (x=x+1) (Move to next MAP boundary)
3374ONTHROTTLE_OR_RPMTOOHIGHFORIDLE:
3375 ldab PointerIntoAdaptiveMemory ; load b with memory contents
3376 inc Temp0 ; Increment Temp0 twice to step the cell index for MAP (map bands represent jumps of 2 cells)
3377 inc Temp0
3378 cpx #DLTMAP_MapHysteresisAtMapCellBoundaries ; -10000100 01001010- (Check if we've hit the end of MAP boundaries)
3379 bne L1245 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
3380L1247: ldaa R1_RPMCellBoundaryInRPMover32 ; load a with memory contents (data is 32) (RPM Threshold separating low/high RPM cells)
3381 lsrb ; logical shift right b
3382 bcs L1248 ; branch if lower
3383 adda DLTRPM_DeltaRPMAtRPMBoundariesInRPMOver32 ; (data is 02) (Add RPM hysteresis)
3384L1248: ldab Temp0 ; load b with memory contents
3385 cmpa EngineRpm_HB ; compare a with memory contents
3386 bcs L1249 ; branch if lower (If RPM > threshold, we stay on the upper cell of this MAP band)
3387 decb ; If RPM < threshold, drop cell index by 1 to hit the lower RPM cell in this band
3388L1249: decb ; Drop one more to compensate for over-incrementing in the loop
3389L1250: cmpb PointerIntoAdaptiveMemory
3390 beq L1251 ; branch if equal (zero)
3391 clr AdaptiveCellUpdateTimer_IncrementedEveryDistRisingEdge ; zero byte at memory location (Reset update timer since we just changed cells)
3392L1251: stab PointerIntoAdaptiveMemory ; store b into memory (Save the calculated cell index)
3393 rts ; return from subroutine
3394

3536; ===========================================================================
3537; DRB II Serial Communications Receiver Routine
3538; Handles baud rate switching, receiving characters, error clearing,
3539; timeout checking, and command parsing for the DRB II diagnostic protocol.
3540; ===========================================================================
3541DRBIISerialCommunications_MM:
3542 jsr CallAndReturn1 ; Call dummy subroutine
3543 jsr BYTE_MODE_SERIAL_CODE_DOWNLOAD_ROUTINE ; Run byte-mode special routine
3544 ldab DRBSerialMode ; Load Serial Mode flags into register B
3545 bitb #bbe_FastSerial | bbe_ByteMode ; Check if FastSerial or ByteMode are active
3546 bne R1255 ; If active, bypass normal DRB processing and return
3547 
3548 ; --- Baud Rate Enforcement ---
3549 ldaa CPU_SerialBaudRate ; Load current baud rate register
3550 anda #0x37 ; Mask to check relevant baud bits
3551 cmpa BAUDLO_DRBBaudRateLo ; Compare against standard DRB low-speed baud rate
3552 beq L1254 ; If already correct, branch to check for received data
3553 ldaa BAUDLO_DRBBaudRateLo ; Load standard DRB baud rate
3554 staa CPU_SerialBaudRate ; Set the baud rate register
3555 rts ; Return to allow baud rate change to take effect
3556 
3557 ; --- Serial Status & Error Handling ---
3558L1254: ldaa CPU_SerialStatus ; Read the SCI status register
3559; staa LEEEE ; (data is ff) - I think this is an error on ChryCo's part. The '90+ code does not have this line...
3560 bita #0x0e ; Check for Overrun, Noise, or Framing errors
3561 beq DRB_NoRxError ; Branch if no errors are present
3562 ldaa CPU_SerialData ; If error exists, read data register to clear the error flags
3563 rts ; Return and wait for next valid byte
3564 
3565 ; --- Receive Data Polling ---
3566DRB_NoRxError:
3567 bita #0x20 ; Check RDRF (Receive Data Register Full) bit
3568 bne DRB_ChrRxd ; If byte received, branch to character processor
3569 
3570 ; --- Timeout Handling ---
3571 brset *DRBSerialMode, #bbe_bottom, DRB_Timeout ; Check if timeout limit reached
3572 incb ; Increment timeout counter (bottom 4 bits of DRBSerialMode)
3573 stab DRBSerialMode ; Store updated timeout counter back
3574 rts ; Return
3575 
3576DRB_Timeout:
3577 brclr *DRBSerialMode, #bbe_TestType3 | bbe_TestType2, R1255 ; If no multi-byte command is pending, just return
3578 bclr *DRBSerialMode, #bbe_TestType3 | bbe_TestType2 ; Clear pending multi-byte test type bits
3579 clr DRBPointer1 ; Reset DRB command pointer 1
3580 rts ; Return
3581 
3582 ; --- Process Received Character ---
3583DRB_ChrRxd:
3584 ldaa CPU_SerialData ; Load the received byte into register A
3585 staa CPU_SerialData ; Echo the byte back (or clear flag)
3586 andb #bbe_top ; Mask out the timeout counter (bottom 4 bits)
3587 stab DRBSerialMode ; Store the cleared timeout counter
3588 bitb #bbe_TestType3 | bbe_TestType2 ; Check if we are waiting for param bytes
3589 bne DRB_StorePointer ; If so, branch to store this byte as a parameter
3590 
3591 ; --- Start of a new DRB Command ---
3592 staa DRBPointer1 ; Store the new command byte into DRBPointer1
3593 clr DRBPointer2 ; Clear the parameter pointer
3594
3595 ; Determine how many parameter bytes this command expects
3596 cmpa #0x1c ; Check if command > 0x1C (Max valid command)
3597 bhi R1255 ; If invalid, return immediately
3598 suba #0x13 ; Subtract offset 0x13
3599 bcs R1255 ; If A < 0x13 (e.g. 0x10, 0x11, 0x12), it's a 1-byte command! Return and process immediately.
3600 bne DRB_SetModeVar ; If A > 0x13, branch to set expected byte counts
3601 
3602 ; Setup ATM Mode checks (Command 0x13)
3603 ldab TimerOverflowsBetweenDistPulses ; Check engine running status
3604 cmpb #0x28 ; Compare against running threshold
3605 bls DRB_SetModeVar ; If engine running, proceed normally
3606 ldab #0x02 ; If not running, force short timeout
3607 stab KeyOnOrEngineRunningTime ; Store timeout
3608 
3609DRB_SetModeVar:
3610 tab ; Transfer offset index to B
3611 ldx #DRBSerialToggles ; Load address of byte-count lookup table
3612 abx ; Add offset to X index
3613 ldab 0x00,x ; Load expected byte count flags from table
3614 orab DRBSerialMode ; OR with current mode
3615 stab DRBSerialMode ; Store updated expected byte count
3616 rts ; Return to wait for parameter bytes
3617 
3618 ; --- Store Command Parameters ---
3619DRB_StorePointer:
3620 bitb #0x20 ; Check if waiting for the 3rd byte (TestType3)
3621 beq DRB_SendMemLocToSCI ; If not, this is the final parameter byte!
3622 staa DRBPointer2 ; Store parameter byte into DRBPointer2
3623 andb #~bbe_TestType3 ; Clear TestType3 flag (move to waiting for final byte)
3624 stab DRBSerialMode ; Update mode
3625R1255: rts ; Return
3626 
3627DRB_SendMemLocToSCI:
3628 andb #~bbe_TestType2 ; Clear TestType2 flag (all bytes received)
3629 stab DRBSerialMode ; Update mode to ready-to-process
3630 ldab DRBPointer1 ; Load the base command byte
3631 cmpb #0x1c ; Check if it is the EMR Reset command
3632 beq DRB_ResetEMR ; Branch to handle EMR Reset
3633 tab ; B = command
3634 ldaa DRBPointer2 ; Load parameter byte into A
3635 xgDX ; X = D (Move parameters to X)
3636 ldaa 0x00,x ; Load memory byte from requested address
3637 jmp SerialOutput1a ; Jump to transmit the memory byte
3638 
3639DRB_ResetEMR:
3640 clr DRBPointer1 ; Clear command pointer
3641 ldab TimerOverflowsBetweenDistPulses ; Check if engine is running
3642 cmpb #0x28 ; Compare engine running threshold
3643 bcs L1257 ; If running, jump to transmit without resetting
3644 sei ; Disable interrupts for safe EEPROM operation
3645 ldab BitFlags_52 ; Load EEPROM/DRB toggle flags
3646 bitb #b52_DRBToggle1 | b52_DRBToggle2 ; Check toggle state
3647 bne L1256 ; If already toggling, skip
3648 bset *BitFlags_52, #b52_DRBToggle1 ; Set toggle 1
3649 cli ; Re-enable interrupts
3650 staa DRBOffsetStored_LB ; Store EMR reset parameters
3651 ldab DRBPointer2 ; Load param 2
3652 stab DRBOffsetStored_HB ; Store param 2
3653 ldaa #0xe2 ; Load 0xE2 success response byte
3654 jmp SerialOutput1a ; Jump to transmit response
3655 
3656L1256: cli ; Re-enable interrupts
3657L1257: jmp SerialOutput1 ; Jump to transmit zero (failure)
3658 
3659; ===========================================================================
3660; DRB II Serial Communications Transmitter Routine
3661; Evaluates DRBPointer1 and jumps to the appropriate handler.
3662; ===========================================================================
3663DRBIIOuput_MM:
3664 ldaa DRBSerialMode ; Load serial mode
3665 bita #bbe_TestType3 | bbe_TestType2 ; Check if still waiting for param bytes
3666 bne R1255 ; If waiting, return (do not process yet)
3667
3668 ; --- Command Processing ---
3669 ldab DRBPointer1 ; Load pending command
3670 subb #0x10 ; Subtract 0x10 to get table offset
3671 bcs R1255 ; If command < 0x10, return
3672 cmpb #0x0c ; Check if command > 0x1C (Max index 0x0C)
3673 bhi R1255 ; If out of bounds, return
3674
3675 ldx #DRBFunctionTable ; Load base address of DRB jump table
3676 lslb ; Multiply offset by 2 (2 bytes per pointer)
3677 abx ; Add offset to table base
3678 ldx 0x00,x ; Load target subroutine address
3679 jmp 0x00,x ; Execute target subroutine
3680 
3681 ; --- DRB Command 0x10: Output Stored Error Codes ---
3682OutputErrorCodes:
3683 ldx #BitFlags_1d ; Point to start of error flag registers
3684 ldab DRBPointer2 ; Load the requested error index
3685 cmpb #0x07 ; Ensure index is within 0-7 bounds
3686 bhi L1258 ; If out of bounds, send end-of-list response
3687 negb ; Calculate exact memory offset
3688 addb #0x07
3689 inx
3690 abx ; Add offset to index
3691 inc DRBPointer2 ; Increment pointer for next request
3692 ldaa 0x00,x ; Load error code byte
3693 bne L1261 ; If non-zero, transmit the error code!
3694L1258: clr DRBPointer1 ; Clear command pointer
3695 ldaa #0xfe ; Load 0xFE (End of Codes indicator)
3696 jsr SerialOutput1a ; Transmit 0xFE

6160INCLUDE_ADAPTIVE_MEMORY:
6161; This routine applies the active AutoCalCell (Adaptive Memory) fuel trim to the calculated Base Fuel PW.
6162; The math works such that each 1 integer unit of the AutoCalCell equals exactly 1/512 (0.1953%) fuel adjustment.
6163 clra ; a = 0 (Initialize high byte of modifier flag to 0)
6164 brset *BitFlags_4f, #b4f_FullThrottle, L1526 ; branch if bit(s) set (If WOT, skip applying adaptive memory, go to L1526 with a=0)

6166 bne L1525 ; branch if not equal (not zero) (If not 0, jump to secondary path for applying adaptives)
6167 ldab ValueFromAdaptiveMemory ; load b with active AutoCalCell modifier (-128 to +127 range)
6168 bmi L1524 ; branch if minus(hi bit 1) (If value is negative, skip incrementing A. A remains 0)
6169L1523: inca ; increment a (If value is positive/zero, A becomes 1 to flag that we should ADD original PW later)
6170L1524: asrb ; Arithmetic shift right B. Halves the value (B/2) while keeping sign. This prepares the 0-255 fractional multiplier.
6171 jsr ScaleXbyB_addingA_intoD ; Call subroutine to calculate: (BasePW * B) / 256. If A=1, it adds BasePW back.
6172 stD *Temp0 ; store D to RAM (Save the newly modified pulse width back into Temp0)
6173 bra L1526 ; branch
6174

6176 bpl L1523 ; branch if plus (hi bit 0) (If positive, jump up to set A=1 and shift)
6177L1526: clra ; a = 0

6179 brclr *EGRVar2, #bit_bit7, L1527 ; branch if bit(s) clear
6180 addb ADMEMA_ValueFromAdaptivememoryAdder1 ; (data is 00)
6181 bvc L1527 ; branch if overflow
6182 ldab #0x7f ; load b with value -01111111-
6183L1527:
6184 tstb
6185 bmi IncludePumpEff ; branch if minus(hi bit 1)
6186 inca ; increment a

7930CalculateSparkAdvance_MM:
7931; Dwell calculation:
7932;
7933; The dwell lookup/calculation is pretty simple.
7934;
7935; First, the ideal dwell period is calculated from the complement of the
7936; lookup value from battery volts. Battery volts is the largest factor for
7937; determining dwell period. The complement is used because the 16-bit
7938; table type cannot have a negative slope.
7939;
7940; Then, the Ditributor PW is compared to the ideal dwell period plus the
7941; the minimum antidwell period. If the dwell + min anti dwell is greater
7942; than the distributor PW, then the minimum antidwell is used. Otherwise,
7943; the ideal dwell is used and the anit-dwell is set to the difference
7944; between the distributor PW and the dwell (floating anti-dwell).
7945;
7946; Logically --> If (DWELL + MINADW) < DISTPW
7947; Then ADWELL = DISTPW - DWELL
7948; Else ADWELL = MINADW
7949 
7950 ldaa BatteryVolts ; load A with memory contents
7951 ldx #DWELL_DwellTimeFromBatteryVoltsComp ; load index with value
7952 jsr Lookup5ByteTable ; call subroutine
7953 coma ; 1's complement A
7954 comb ; 1's complement B
7955 std DwellTime_HB
7956

9166; ********************************************************
9167; Scale Y by A, where a=0 = 0.0 and a=255 = ~0.996 (255/256)
9168;*************************************************************
9169;
9170; Inputs: A = Unsigned fractional multiplier (0-255 representing 0/256 to 255/256)
9171; Y = 16-bit value to be scaled (e.g. Base Fuel PW)
9172;
9173; Outputs:Y = scaled value (Y * A / 256)
9174;
9175; Pimarily used by the fueling system to calculate an
9176; interpolated point into one of the 5-byte tables. The base
9177; value of the break point will be added to the returned result
9178; of this routine to make the new interpolated return value.
9179; It is also heavily used to scale fuel pulse widths by adaptive multipliers.
9180;
9181;*************************************************************
9182 
9183ScaleYbyA:
9184 psha ; save a copy of the multiplier (A) on the stack
9185 pshy ; save a copy of the 16-bit value (Y) on the stack
9186 pulb ; put the high byte of the 16-bit value (Y_hi) into B
9187 mul ; multiply the multiplier (A) by Y_hi. Result is in D (16-bit).
9188 xgDY ; store the 16-bit result from D to Y. (Y now holds A * Y_hi)
9189 pulb ; get the fractional low byte of the 16-bit value (Y_lo) into B
9190 pula ; retrieve stored copy of the multiplier (A) from stack
9191 mul ; multiply A by Y_lo, 16-bit result is in D (A * Y_lo)
9192 adca #0x00 ; add carry to A (which contains the high byte of A * Y_lo, equivalent to (A * Y_lo) / 256)
9193 tab ; move A to B
9194 aby ; Add B to Y. Y now holds: (A * Y_hi) + ((A * Y_lo) / 256). This equals Y * A / 256.
9195 rts ; return from subroutine
9196 
9197; ********************************************************
9198; Scales the 16-bit value at memory location X (not X itself) by B
9199; If a=1 adds original 16-bit value (1.0) to the scaled result
9200; Calculates: Result = (Value_at_X * B / 256) + (a == 1 ? Value_at_X : 0)
9201 
9202ScaleXbyB_addingA_intoD:
9203 psha ; push the add-flag (A) onto stack
9204 tba ; Move the fractional multiplier (B) into A for ScaleYbyA
9205 ldY 0, X ; load the 16-bit value (Base PW) indexed by X into Y
9206 bsr ScaleYbyA ; call subroutine to scale Y by A. Y becomes (Y * A / 256)
9207 pula ; pull the add-flag (A) from stack
9208 tsta ; test a to see if it is 0 or 1
9209 xgDY ; exchange D and Y (D now holds the scaled result)
9210 beq R1828 ; branch if equal (zero). If A=0, return just the scaled fractional result.
9211 addd 0x00,x ; If A=1, add the original 16-bit value (at X) to D. D = original + scaled fraction.
9212 bcc R1828 ; branch if no overflow occurred
9213 ldd #0xffff ; If overflowed, max out D to 0xFFFF (65535)
9214R1828: rts ; return from subroutine
9215 
9216; ********************************************************
9217; X points to either the MAP or TPS 4-byte block.
9218; block of 4 bytes: x+0: MSB of average value
9219; x+1: LSB of average value (scratch, never used)
9220; x+2: actual value (or faked if limpin)
9221; x+3: scaling factor for leanout or enrichment
9222; flow:
9223; if scaling=0, save value into first byte, zero second, and return
9224; otherwise:
9225; scale average value by scaling factor
9226 
9227 
9228ProcessMapOrTpsBlockData:
9229 ldaa 0x03,x ; load a with current averaging factor
9230 bne L1829 ; branch if not equal (not zero)
9231 clrb ; b = 0
9232 ldaa 0x02,x ; load a with actual MAP or TPS value
9233 bra L1830 ; store average MAP or TPS value, in this case = same as actual, since the averaging factor = 0
9234 
9235L1829: ldY 0, X ; load Y with the current average MAP or TPS
9236 bsr ScaleYbyA ; scale the average MAP or TPS by the averaging factor
9237 pshy ; push the scaled current average MAP/TPS onto the stack
9238 ldd 0x02,x ; load a with the actual MAP value, b with the averaging factor
9239 mul ; multiply the MAP/TPS by the averaging factor, product ends up in D
9240 tSY ; load Y with the address of the LB of the scaled current average MAP value
9241 subD 0, Y ; subtract scaled current average from the product, delta stays in D
9242 puly ; get scaled current average from the stack (just to clear the stack)
9243 addd 0x00,x ; add the scaled current average to the delta
9244L1830: std 0x00,x ; store the new average to memory
9245 rts ; return from subroutine

10088;

10092; time through the main loop these bits are copied to the
10093; actual hardware.
10094;
10095; To enable this code, simply check the Custom Options flag for it
10096; in the table file. This codebase has been modified to check for
10097; the option and will automatically re-config the SMEC appropriately.
10098;

10104 ldaa CoolantTemp
10105 cmpa KNKMIN_FlashCEMinTemp

10107 ldaa Cylinder2Retard ; load a with memory contents
10108 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10109 ldaa Cylinder1Retard ; load a with memory contents
10110 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10111 ldaa Cylinder3Retard ; load a with memory contents
10112 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10113 ldaa Cylinder4Retard ; load a with memory contents
10114 bne KnockDetect_LightCEL ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10115NoKnockDetect_UnlightCEL: ; fallthrough, extinguish light
10116 bset *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_CELight
10117 bra FlashCEL_OnKnock_return
10118KnockDetect_LightCEL:
10119 bclr *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_CELight

10207; -------------------------------------------------------
10208; Anti-Lag Retard Routine
10209; -------------------------------------------------------
10210CalculateSparkCutandAntiLagRetard_Routine:
10211
10212 ; ******************************************************************
10213 ; Called from the falling edge interrupt sevice routine...
10214 ; on entry and exit, accA contains the total timing (don't use accA for anything else in this routine!)
10215 ; if anti-lag should be on, substitute the antilag value for the total timing
10216 ; otherwise return the original
10217
10218 ; Rotating spark cut:
10219 ; 2 address tables, one containing the 'value', 1 the 'base';
10220 ; 'base' is used to count (counter init)
10221 ; 'value' is rotated (ROLx), the result in carry is used to determine if the cylinder should be allowed to fire this time.
10222 ; When the count = base, then reset the counter and reload the pattern
10223 ;
10224 ; The 'Spark Cut Fraction' value is now simply a pointer to the pattern and counter base.
10225 
10226 ; Patterns:
10227 
10228 ; 1/3 - 011 00000; index = 0; value = 96(0x60); base = 3+1
10229 ; 2/3 - 001 00000; index = 1; value = 32(0x20); base = 3+1
10230 ; 3/5 - 00101 000; index = 2; value = 40(0x28); base = 5+1
10231 ; 4/5 - 01000 000; index = 3; value = 64(0x40); base = 5+1
10232 ; 3/7 - 0011011 0; index = 4; value = 54(0x36); base = 7+1
10233 ; 4/7 - 0010101 0; index = 5; value = 42(0x2a); base = 7+1
10234 ; 5/7 - 0010001 0; index = 6; value = 34(0x22); base = 7+1
10235 ; 6/7 - 0001000 0; index = 7; value = 16(0x10); base = 7+1
10236
10237 ; Other patterns or modified patterns are also possible.
10238 
10239 ; ******************************************************************
10240 ; check spark and anti-lag enable conditions
10241 
10242 ldx #Turbonator_Flags
10243 bclr 0x00, x, #Turbonator_AntiLag ; clear the antilag flag since it hasn't been determined yet
10244 bset 0x00, x, #Turbonator_AllowSpark ; spark is allowed normally
10245 brclr 0x00, x, #Turbonator_Staging, AntiLag_Return ; don't do anything unless we're staging, normal spark
10246 brclr 0x00, x, #Turbonator_SparkCut, CalulateLaunchAdvance ; branch if the spark cut isn't on right now - check for anti-lag conditions since we are staging
10247 bclr 0x00, x, #Turbonator_AllowSpark ; spark cut is on, so clear the 'allow' flag
10248 
10249RotateSparkCutPattern:
10250 ; counter works because this routine is called from the rising edge routine - once per cylinder
10251 ldab Counter_SparkCut
10252 beq SetBaseandPattern
10253 dec Counter_SparkCut
10254 rol Pattern_SparkCut ; if we should have spark, then the carry bit will be set after the rotate
10255 bcc CalulateLaunchAdvance ; if carry is now set, then allow spark...
10256 
10257AllowSparkThisRotation:
10258 bset 0x00, x, #Turbonator_AllowSpark ; allow spark for just this revolution...
10259 
10260 ; check that antilag is enabled
10261 
10262CalulateLaunchAdvance:
10263 ldx #OPTN2_CalCustomOptionConfigFlags2
10264 brclr 0x00, X, #opt_AntiLag, AntiLag_Return
10265 
10266 ldab ANLGRP_AntiLagRetardRPM
10267 cmpb EngineRpm_HB
10268 bcc AntiLag_Return ; branch if

10273 ldx #Turbonator_Flags
10274 bset 0x00, x, #Turbonator_AntiLag ;just to indicate that the anti-lag is active, for logging purposes
10275 
10276AntiLag_Return:
10277 rts

10368; -------------------------------------------------------
10369; PTU (Lock-Up Converter) Control Routine
10370; -------------------------------------------------------
10371;
10372; This code is largely copied over from the TBI SMEC code. It is very similar to
10373; the code used in the '90/91 SBEC T1 cars that have PTU from the factory. The table
10374; and constant values (defined above) are the same as the 'leftover' PTU data included
10375; with the SMEC T1 cals and as the working SBEC T1 cals.
10376;
10377; There is an output overlap between the PTU output and the EMR. So, the EMR code will
10378; have to be dis-abled if built using the PTU output control.
10379 
10380ControlPTU_MM:
10381 ldab CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags ; load b with memory contents (data is bf)
10382 bitb #cfg_PTU ; -00010000-
10383 beq LD4DF ; branch if equal (zero)
10384 jmp PTU_Main
10385 
10386LD4DF: ldaa ATMOffset ; load a with memory contents
10387 cmpa #0x16 ; compare a with value -00010110-
10388 beq LD4E9 ; branch if equal (zero)
10389 cmpa #0x14 ; compare a with value -00010100-
10390 bne PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10391LD4E9: rts ; return from subroutine
10392 
10393PTU_Main:
10394 ldaa PTU_MapTemp ; load a with memory contents
10395 staa Temp0 ; store a into memory
10396 ldaa Counter_MainLoop ; load a with memory contents
10397 anda PTUCNI_PTUCounterTimerIntervalForLoop ; (data is 07)
10398 bne PTU_CheckThrottleForLock ; branch if not equal (not zero)
10399 ldaa MapValue ; load a with memory contents
10400 staa PTU_MapTemp ; store a into memory
10401 
10402PTU_CheckThrottleForLock:
10403 ldaa TpsVolts ; load a with memory contents
10404 suba MINTHR_LowestSessionTPS
10405 bls PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if lower or same
10406 staa Temp4 ; store a into memory
10407 ldaa CoolantTemp ; load a with memory contents
10408 cmpa PTUMTP_PTUMinLockTemperature ; compare a with memory contents (data is c5)
10409 bcs PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if lower
10410 brclr *BitFlags_AIS, #b0c_ATXInGear, PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if bit(s) clear
10411 brset *StartupSwitchMirror1, #sw1_Brake, PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if bit(s) set
10412 ldd VehicleSpeed_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
10413 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10414 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10415 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10416 cmpa PTUMSP_PTUMinLockSpeed ; compare a with memory contents (data is 68)
10417 bcc PTU_CheckMAPThresholdsForLock ; branch if greater or equal
10418 ldaa MapValue ; load a with memory contents
10419 suba Temp0
10420 bcs PTU_CheckMAPThresholdsForLock ; branch if lower
10421 cmpa PTUMP3_PTUMAPThresholdForLock3 ; compare a with memory contents (data is 20)
10422 bcc PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if greater or equal
10423 bra LD63A ; branch
10424 
10425PTU_SetPTUBits:
10426 clra ; a = 0
10427 staa Counter_PartThrottleUnlock ; store a into memory
10428 bset *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_PartThrotUnlock ; set bits
10429 bclr *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_B | b52_PTU_A ; clear bits
10430 rts ; return from subroutine
10431 
10432PTU_CheckMAPThresholdsForLock:
10433 ldaa Temp0 ; load a with memory contents
10434 suba MapValue
10435 bcs LD63A ; branch if lower
10436 staa Temp0 ; store a into memory
10437 ldx #PTUMP1_PTUMAPThresholdForLock1 ; load index with value
10438 brset *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_B, LD632 ; branch if bit(s) set
10439 brset *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_A, LD631 ; branch if bit(s) set
10440 ldaa Temp4 ; load a with memory contents
10441 cmpa PTUDTP_PTUDeltaTPSForUnlock ; compare a with memory contents (data is 26)
10442 bcs LD62E ; branch if lower
10443 bset *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_B ; set bits
10444 bra LD632 ; branch
10445 
10446LD62E: bset *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_A ; set bits
10447LD631: inx ; increment index (x=x+1)
10448LD632: ldab Temp0 ; load b with memory contents
10449 cmpb 0x00,x
10450 bcc PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if greater or equal
10451 bra PTU_CheckCounter ; branch
10452 
10453LD63A: bclr *BitFlags_52, #b52_PTU_B | b52_PTU_A ; clear bits
10454PTU_CheckCounter:
10455 ldaa Counter_PartThrottleUnlock ; load a with memory contents
10456 cmpa #0x01 ; compare a with value -00000001-
10457 bls PTU_CheckThresholdsForUnlock ; branch if lower or same
10458 deca ; decrement a
10459 staa Counter_PartThrottleUnlock ; store a into memory
10460 rts ; return from subroutine
10461 
10462PTU_CheckThresholdsForUnlock:
10463 ldx #PTUUUL_UpperLimitForPTUUnlock ; load index with value
10464 brclr *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_PartThrotUnlock, LD651 ; branch if bit(s) clear
10465 ldx #PTULUL_UpperLimitForPTULock ; load index with value
10466LD651: bsr PTU_LookupPTUParam ; call subroutine
10467 bcc PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if Temp4 (Delta TPS) < lookup value
10468 ldx #PTUULL_LowerLimitForPTUUnlock ; load index with value
10469 brclr *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_PartThrotUnlock, LD65F ; branch if bit(s) clear
10470 ldx #PTULLL_LowerLimitForPTULock ; load index with value
10471LD65F: bsr PTU_LookupPTUParam ; call subroutine
10472 bcs PTU_SetPTUBits ; branch if Temp4 (DeltaTPS) > lookup value
10473 ldaa Counter_PartThrottleUnlock ; load a with memory contents
10474 beq PTU_CheckVehicleSpeed ; branch if equal (zero)
10475 bclr *PIA1_A_Buffer, #pia1abuf_PartThrotUnlock ; clear bits
10476 rts ; return from subroutine
10477 
10478PTU_CheckVehicleSpeed:
10479 ldd VehicleSpeed_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
10480 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10481 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10482 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10483 ldab PTUCNH_PTUCounterHiSpeed ; load b with memory contents (data is 5b)
10484 cmpa PTUMSP_PTUMinLockSpeed ; compare a with memory contents (data is 68)
10485 bcc LD67B ; branch if greater or equal
10486 ldab PTUCNL_PTUCounterLoSpeed ; load b with memory contents (data is b5)
10487LD67B: stab Counter_PartThrottleUnlock ; store b into memory
10488 rts ; return from subroutine
10489 
10490PTU_LookupPTUParam:
10491 ldd VehicleSpeed_HB ; load d (a&b) with memory contents
10492 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10493 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10494 asld ; shift left (d=d*2)
10495 jsr Lookup4ByteTable ; call subroutine
10496 ldaa Temp4 ; load a with memory contents
10497 cba ; set the flags as if A-B
10498 rts ; return from subroutine

10506; configurable by the user/calibrator.

10508; Here's how I think this should work:
10509;
10510; 1) 2 setpoints for the shift light; 1 for 1st gear, one for all other gears
10511; 2) adjustable by the driver - special mode?
10512; - special mode: when the engine is not running, press and hold the brake pedal, push cruise set (?) button
10513; - to increment the shift light point; display the value on the tach?
10514; 3) option to flash the light 3 times before the shift, based on rpm
10515; 4) user/calibrator selectable output (cruise solenoids, purge solenoids, egr solenoid, or PTU output, EMR output, etc.)
10516; 5) will require 2 routines; 1 for running the light, the other for setup.
10517

10529; ; then press throttle to indicate shift rpm on tach and press brake again to set
10530; ; to set 2nd point, press brake 4 times in 2 sec, otherwise same procedure...

10532; ; need to figure out how to time the tach pulses to do this right, might be difficult to do

10537; bra ShiftLight_Return

10548; ShiftLight_TurnLightOff:

10554; ********************************
10555; Alky Injection Control Routines
10556; ********************************
10557;
10558; ********************
10559; pump control routine
10560; ********************
10561;
10562; MM_AlkyPump_Control:
10563;
10564; ldaa CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
10565; bita #cfg_AlkyInj ; check the bit for Alky Injection
10566; beq AlkyPump_Return ; branch if the bit is not set, ie not enabled
10567; bita #cfg_SpeedSenseAero ; check the bit for Speed Sensitive Aero
10568; bne AlkyPump_Return ; branch if the bit is set, can't run both of these routines
10569;
10570; ldaa MapValue
10571; ldab Z83_PortA_copy
10572; cmpa AKPMON_AlkyPumpOnSetpointFromMAP
10573; bcs AlkyPump_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
10574; orab #PortA_PurgeEGR ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on the pump
10575; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10576; jmp AlkyPump_Return
10577;
10578; AlkyPump_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
10579; cmpa AKPMOF_AlkyPumpOffSetpointFromMAP
10580; bcc AlkyPump_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
10581; andb ~#PortA_PurgeEGR ;turn off the pump
10582; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10583;
10584; AlkyPump_Return:
10585; rts
10586;
10587; ************************
10588; injector control routine
10589; ************************
10590; ; these are just messages to display during assemble to let you know what's going on...
10591;
10592; MM_AlkyInjector_Control:
10593;
10594; first, check to see if inj1 is already on, if it is, then check to see if it needs to be turned off, then maybe check inj2 turn on
10595; ldaa CONFIG_ConfigurationFlags
10596; bita #cfg_AlkyInj ; check the bit for Alky Injection
10597; beq AlkyInj_Return ; branch if the bit is not set, ie not enabled
10598; bita #cfg_SpeedSenseAero ; check the bit for Speed Sensitive Aero
10599; bne AlkyInj_Return ; branch if the bit is set, can't run both of these routines
10600;
10601; ldab Z83_PortA_copy
10602; orab #PortA_CruiseVent ;clear all bits in A except for this one
10603; andb #PortA_CruiseVent
10604; bne AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;branch if the bit for inj1 is set
10605;
10606; inj1 is not already on, so check the MAP level
10607;
10608; ldaa MapValue
10609; cmpa AKI1ON_AlkyInj1OnSetpointFromMAP
10610; bcs AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
10611; orab #PortA_CruiseVent ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on inj 1
10612; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10613; jmp AlkyInj_Return
10614;
10615; AlkyInj1_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
10616; cmpa AKI1OF_AlkyInj1OffSetpointFromMAP
10617; bcc AlkyInj_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
10618; andb ~#PortA_CruiseVent ;turn off inj 1
10619; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10620;
10621; AlkyInj_CheckInj2:
10622; ldaa MapValue
10623; cmpa AKI2ON_AlkyInj2OnSetpointFromMAP
10624; bcs AlkyInj2_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff ;if MAP is lower than the setpoint, see if it's lower than the 'off' point
10625; orab #PortA_CruiseVac ;or whichever output you're going to use, this sets the bit to turn on inj 2
10626; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10627; jmp AlkyInj_Return
10628;
10629; AlkyInj2_CheckHysteresisAndTurnOff:
10630; cmpa AKI2OF_AlkyInj2OffSetpointFromMAP
10631; bcc AlkyInj_Return ; MAP is still higher than the 'off' setpoint
10632; andb ~#PortA_CruiseVac ;turn off inj 1
10633; stab Z83_PortA_copy
10634;
10635; AlkyInj_Return:
10636; rts

10698; Quick 68HC11 reference:
10699; a Accumulator A (8-bit)
10700; b Accumulator B (8-bit)
10701; d A and B combined (16-bit, A hi, B lo)
10702; ccr Condition Code Register (8-bit, CCR)
10703; pc Program Counter (16-bit)
10704; sp Stack Pointer (16-bit)
10705; ix Index Register X (16-bit)
10706; iy Index Register Y (16-bit)
10707;
10708; some RAM bytes from 0000 are kept alive by standby battery power.
10709;
10710; 0000 to 00ff - 256 bytes of internal RAM
10711; ffd6 to ffff - Interrupt vectors (TechRef Chapter 5)
10712; ------------
10713; ffd6 to ffd7 - SCI Interrupt vector: b33a
10714; ffd8 to ffd9 - SPIE Flag Interrupt vector: b33a
10715; ffda to ffdb - PAII Flag Interrupt vector: b308
10716; ffdc to ffdd - PAOVI Flag Interrupt vector: b2f6
10717; ffde to ffdf - TOI Flag Interrupt vector: b33a
10718; ffe0 to ffe1 - OC5 Flag Interrupt vector: bd17
10719; ffe2 to ffe3 - OC4 Flag Interrupt vector: b305
10720; ffe4 to ffe5 - OC3 Flag Interrupt vector: b302
10721; ffe6 to ffe7 - OC2 Flag Interrupt vector: c7c6
10722; ffe8 to ffe9 - OC1 Timer Interrupt vector: 8900
10723; ffea to ffeb - IC3 Timer Interrupt vector: b2ff
10724; ffec to ffed - IC2 Timer Interrupt vector: bdad
10725; ffee to ffef - IC1 Timer Interrupt vector: ae92
10726; fff0 to fff1 - Realtime Interrupt vector: b33a
10727; fff2 to fff3 - IRQ hardware Interrupt vector: c49d
10728; fff4 to fff5 - XIRQ hardware Interrupt vector: b2f0
10729; fff6 to fff7 - SWI Software Interrupt vector: b2ed
10730; fff8 to fff9 - Illegal Opcode vector: b2f9
10731; fffa to fffb - COP Watchdog Timeout vector: b2f3
10732; fffc to fffd - Clock Monitor Fail vector: b2fc
10733; fffe to ffff - Power on or external Reset vector: b33a
10734; ------------
10735
